declared.title: Randomized Controlled Trial of a Volitional Help Sheet to Encourage Weight Loss in the Middle East
declared.foundIn: reports/choose-your-struggle/counter-evidence.md (card 18); Crossref search « Armitage Alganem Norman implementation intentions weight loss Kuwait randomized » (2026-11-26)

population: 216 overweight or obese adults (127 women, 61 men, 28 not stated) joining a commercial weight-loss program in Kuwait; nationality not reported

findings.text: Linking critical situations to responses as if-then plans on a help sheet led to more weight lost at 6 months (clinic records) than ticking the same situations and responses without linking them

support.sentence: Participants in the intervention condition lost significantly more weight (6.15 kg; -6.58% initial body weight) than those in the control condition (3.66 kg; -4.04% initial body weight), M diff = 2.55% initial body weight, SE diff = .92, t(214) = 2.76, p = .006, 95%CI = .73, 4.36, d = .38.

limits: if-then plans alone, without mental contrasting, wish or image of the result: one half of WOOP, against listing the same situations
unequal dropout (25 control, 14 intervention), analysed with baseline weight carried forward: a dropout counts as 0 kg lost, which favours the arm that loses fewer
no protocol or analysis plan published before; simple randomization by coin toss (119 vs 97); 23% of the people approached accepted
the 10% weight-loss result (22.7% vs 14.4%) is reported as p = .062: a one-tailed value (two-tailed about .12)
one paying commercial program (people already set on losing weight), 2010; weight from clinic records, staff blind to condition
a sample in Kuwait, questionnaires translated into Arabic and back-translated; nationality and language of the participants not reported
allegiance: Armitage introduced the volitional help sheet (Health Psychology, 2008) and has tested it several times since; he is also a co-author of cole-2021-simulation
